title: Grant Calendar access
intro: Two minutes, sir. One command, one Allow click, and I can see your actual calendar.

steps.title: Why this is needed
steps.body: The morning run reads Calendar.app through a small helper. macOS only shows the permission prompt to a real app like Terminal; my build sandbox could not present it, so calendar status is stuck on denied.
steps.voice: Step one, context. macOS wants you, not me, to click the permission prompt.

steps.title: Run the helper in Terminal
steps.body: Open Terminal (the real Terminal app) and run the command below. A macOS prompt should appear: Terminal would like to access your calendar. Click Allow, and choose Full Access if offered.
steps.voice: Step two. Run the calendar helper in Terminal and click Allow when macOS asks.

steps.title: If no prompt appeared
steps.body: System Settings, Privacy and Security, Calendars: set Terminal to Full Access, then run the command from step two again.
steps.voice: Step three, only if the prompt never showed. Grant Terminal calendar access in System Settings and run it again.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Run the check below. status should read ok and today's events list out. The HUD core panel picks them up on the next refresh, and every 7:30 briefing routes the day around real appointments from now on.
steps.voice: Step four. Check the calendar file says status ok. Then we are done, sir.

outro: Calendar sighted. The day plan just got honest.
